or_great_arch_the.blurb: The Great Arch is the main sport wall on Wolf Rock, the biggest freestanding rock in Oregon, tucked in the Cascade foothills east of Eugene in the Willamette Valley region. Nineteen routes are recorded here, almost all of them bolted single pitches with a pair of trad lines mixed in. The grades lean hard toward the 5.10s, with a good handful of 5.11s, a few 5.9s, and just a couple of easier lines in the 5.7 range. That makes it better suited to climbers who already lead the middle grades than to true beginners. Expect a remote forest crag feel rather than a roadside crowd scene.

or_blobby_zone.blurb: Blobby Zone is a small bouldering patch at Cline Falls, on the Deschutes River a few miles west of Redmond in Central Oregon. It is basically three boulders plus a few problems along the low bluff beside them, and it sits just upstream of another named boulder cluster. The 18 problems cover the full range from easy V0 warm-ups through the middle grades to a handful of harder V4 to V6 lines, with the single biggest group at the easy end. Problems are short, around ten feet, so one or two pads are plenty. A quick stop that pairs well with the rest of the Cline Falls boulders.

or_1_bone_yard.blurb: Bone Yard is a compact alcove at the far west end of the Terra Nova crag in Southwest Oregon, reached by walking along the upper edge of the cliff. All 18 routes are bolted single pitches, up to about 80 feet, so a standard sport rack and a long rope are enough. The grade spread is concentrated: a dozen routes sit in the 5.11 range, a few go into 5.12, and only a small number are easier, so this is a place for climbers already comfortable on steeper, harder sport. The longer 5.11s are on the west wall. The setting is quiet and scenic, but the trail near the end is faint.
or_1_bone_yard.approach: Walk along the top of the crag past several other walls. The trail fades near the end, so scramble up a short dirt slab for a few feet to reach the alcove.

or_5_shakespeare_cliff.blurb: Shakespeare Cliff is a basalt crag in the Lower Gorge of Smith Rock State Park, on the far side of the Crooked River from the busy main walls. Most of its 18 routes are trad, and the character is crack climbing: finger cracks, hand jams and short roofs, with a few bolted lines at the harder end. Grades run from around 5.7 up to 5.11, spread fairly evenly through the 5.9 to 5.11 range, so there is something for solid intermediates. The river crossing and walk in keep crowds thinner than on the famous faces. Route names borrow from Shakespeare plays.
or_5_shakespeare_cliff.approach: Walk the main path down to the river and over the bridge, then follow the river trail into the Lower Gorge and cross the water to the cliff.

or_shining_wall.blurb: Shining Wall is the cliff you can spot from the parking area at Madrone Wall, a basalt crag in the Portland area. Of its 18 routes, most are trad and a handful are bolted. The wall is steeply undercut, and the grades cluster around 5.10 and 5.11 with a few 5.9s and one 5.8 at the bottom end, plus a single 5.12. It faces the sun for most of the day, which makes it uncomfortable in summer heat but a pleasant, warm place to climb on a clear winter day. Bring a trad rack for most lines.

or_yellow_wall.blurb: Yellow Wall is a sector of Carver Cliff, east of Portland near Gresham, best recognised by a big yellow slab topped with a roof. The 18 routes split roughly evenly between trad and bolted lines, with one top-rope. Grades run widely, from a few low-angle fourth-class and easy 5th class pitches up to several 5.13 testpieces, with the largest group in the 5.8 to 5.11 range. That breadth makes it a good all-rounder wall: moderate trad for building skills, mid-grade sport for volume and a few hard lines to aim at. It holds some of the most sought-after routes at Carver.
